nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Intense desert sun drives plant growth but also the summer heat and drought that limit it.

nodes.name: Scarce rainfall
nodes.desc: The Karakum gets only about 70 to 150 mm of rain a year, so a short spring flush of annual plants matters a great deal.

nodes.name: Sandy soil and dunes
nodes.desc: Loose sand holds little organic matter. Deep-rooted shrubs help anchor it, and returning nutrients feed the plants.

nodes.name: Groundwater
nodes.desc: Deep-rooted desert shrubs tap water below the sand surface, which lets them survive long dry spells. General ecology.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Soil algae, fungi and bacteria break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the sand.

nodes.name: Black saxaul
nodes.desc: A leafless desert tree of sandy deserts that forms saxaul woodland in Central Asia and is the signature plant of the reserve. Locusts and beetles attack it.

nodes.name: White saxaul
nodes.desc: A shrubby saxaul of shifting sands, one of the best-recorded plants in the area.

nodes.name: Calligonum shrubs
nodes.desc: Sand-loving shrubs with thin, nearly leafless stems that grow on dunes of the Karakum.

nodes.name: Spring annual grasses
nodes.desc: Short-lived grasses and herbs that sprout after rain and set seed quickly, a seasonal feast for seed and leaf eaters.

nodes.name: Goitered gazelle
nodes.desc: A vulnerable desert antelope of sands and gravel plains, with a significant population in the reserve. Herds travel to find food.

nodes.name: Great gerbil
nodes.desc: A colonial burrowing rodent of Central Asian deserts that eats plant material. It is prey for reptiles, owls and foxes.

nodes.name: Saxaul locusts
nodes.desc: Locusts of this genus are recorded as pests of saxaul in Turkmenistan and neighbouring countries.

nodes.name: Darkling beetles
nodes.desc: Hardy ground beetles of sandy deserts that feed on plant matter and debris, and feed many lizards and birds.

nodes.name: Saxaul sparrow
nodes.desc: A small sparrow tied to saxaul and desert shrubs that eats seeds and some insects. Prey for shrikes, owls and snakes.

nodes.name: Common wonder gecko
nodes.desc: A nocturnal gecko of sand dunes that shelters in a deep burrow by day and eats insects and other lizards.

nodes.name: Steppe agama
nodes.desc: A common desert lizard that hunts insects by day. It is recorded as prey of the steppe ribbon racer.

nodes.name: Steppe ribbon racer
nodes.desc: A slender, fast snake of sandy deserts that eats lizards such as the steppe agama.

nodes.name: Turkestan ground jay
nodes.desc: A ground-living crow of sandy desert with low shrubs, and the best-recorded bird near the reserve. Forages on the ground.

nodes.name: Great grey shrike
nodes.desc: A songbird predator that takes large insects, small rodents, lizards and small birds, and impales surplus prey on thorns.

nodes.name: Little owl
nodes.desc: A small owl that eats insects and small vertebrates, including mammals, reptiles and birds.

nodes.name: Desert monitor
nodes.desc: A large burrowing lizard that eats mammals, reptiles, birds, eggs and insects, and also feeds on carrion. The reserve is known for it.

nodes.name: Caspian cobra
nodes.desc: A venomous snake of dry scrub that mainly eats small mammals, and also takes birds and other snakes.

nodes.name: Corsac fox
nodes.desc: A small steppe and desert fox named among Karakum mammals. Eats rodents and insects. General ecology.
